Permian remagnetization of the Early Cambrian Guachos Formation,
Eastern Cordillera, Argentina
Pablo R. Franceschinisa,b,*, Sabrina Y. Fazzitoa,b, Augusto E. Rapalinia,b, Mo ´ nica P. Escayolab,c,
Silvana E. Geunaa,b, Constanza Rodríguez Picedad,e
aUniversidad de Buenos Aires, Laboratorio de Paleomagnetismo Daniel A. Valencio, Instituto de Geociencias Ba´sicas, Aplicadas y Ambientales de Buenos Aires (IGEBA),
Departamento de Ciencias Geol´ogicas, Facultad de Ciencias Exactas y Naturales, Argentina
bCONICET, Argentina
cICPA-Universidad Nacional de Tierra del Fuego, Anta´rtida e Islas del Atla´ntico Sur, Argentina
dInstitut für Geowissenschaften, Universita¨t Potsdam, Potsdam, Germany
eGFZ – German Research Center for Geosciences, Potsdam, Germany
A R T I C L E I N F O A B S T R A C T
Keywords: The Permian remagnetization belt that affects the southwestern margin of Gondwana has an important
Guachos formation geographic extension reaching several South American cratons and terranes. A paleomagnetic pole for the Early
Remagnetization Cambrian Guachos Formation in the Eastern Cordillera of Argentina was computed (LG: Lat: 58.1◦S, Long:
Paleomagnetism 20.2◦E, A95: 6.4◦, n: 30), that likely corresponds to a Permian remagnetization and suggests that such belt might
extend further north than previously envisaged. We performed several rock-magnetic studies on this succession
of laminated fine grain sandstones and siltstones in order to determine the magnetic phases that carry the
remanence. Thermomagnetic (k vs. T) curves, field and frequency dependence of bulk susceptibility, hysteresis
loops, isothermal remanent magnetization acquisition and back-field curves, three-axis IRM thermal demagne-
tization, among others, permitted to establish magnetite as the main mineral carrying the remanence. Micro-
scopic observations confirmed a secondary chemical origin for magnetite. Magnetic fabric studies indicate a
tectonic fabric, consistent with cleavage developed on these rocks together with low-grade metamorphism.
However, a Permian remagnetization, as suggested by the paleomagnetic pole position, cannot be related to
Cambrian deformation and metamorphism and might be related to hydrothermal processes.
1. Introduction this regional remagnetization relates this event to the orogenic processes
that affected the southwestern margin of Gondwana in the Permian, i.e.

### page_9
P.R. Franceschinis et al. J o u r n a l o f S o u t h A m e r i c a n E a r t h S c i e n c e s 106(2021)102887
et al., 2018; Franceschinis et al., 2020) few tens of km to the north and
south of the study location did not show evidence of significant tectonic
rotations. The regular regional trend of the main anticlinal structure of
the Sierra de Mojotoro shows no important deflection at the sampling
locality, so that a large tectonic rotation due to Andean orogeny seems
unlikely. This suggests an Early Permian remagnetization for the Gua-
chos Formation. Our rock magnetic data and petrographic analyses plus
the magnetic fabrics results clearly indicate that secondary magnetite
due to chemical precipitation carries this remanence and suggest a
Permian age for such an event. No previous reports of Late Paleozoic
remagnetization are known from the Eastern Cordillera on NW
Argentina. The unique reverse polarity found in the studied samples also
is consistent with the Late Carboniferous-Early Permian Kiaman Reverse
Polarity Superchron (Gradstein et al., 2012), and therefore with the
inferred age of remagnetization.
Magnetite is confirmed by different rock-magnetic experiments as
the main carrier of magnetic remanence in the Guachos Formation.
Subordinate hematite was also identified and is probably associated
with martitization of magnetite crystals, as seen in the microscope. The
presence of SD plus MD magnetite was also indicated by the rock

However, the fact that the microscopic observations and the magnetic
fabrics suggest that magnetite crystallization was probably associated
with the development of tectonic fabric and cleavage in these rocks is
not easily reconciled with a Permian age as suggested from the paleo-
magnetic pole position. Low grade metamorphism in Guachos Forma-
tion occurred in Early Cambrian times, linked to the final stages of the
Tilcaric orogenic phase (Moya, 1998). The simplest explanation for the
tectonic overprint is to assign it an age older than the ca. 500 Ma
unmetamorphosed Meson Group that overlies it. Although no major
Andean tectonic rotations around vertical axes are expected for the
sampling locality, as already discussed, the likelihood of older rotations
should be analyzed. Fig. 13 illustrates the expected paleolatitude for the
sampling locality from the Early Cambrian to the Middle Triassic based
on the Gondwana reference APWP (Torsvik et al., 2012, Fig. 12) and that
inferred from the Guachos Formation mean characteristic remanence.
From this, it is evident that a very large discrepancy in paleolatitude is
observed for most of the Paleozoic. In particular, the Early Cambrian
expected paleolatitude is over 30◦ higher than that observed at the
Guachos Formation. Besides the Permian, only Early to Middle Ordo-
vician Gondwana pole positions show consistent paleolatitudes. How-
